messages:
Lina (sec-engineer): Kicking off design thread: AWS KMS for Redwood Private (VPC). main goals: clear RBAC, auditability, BYOK onboarding, rotation tooling. thoughts?
Rahul (infra): +1. high-level: separate CMKs for control-plane (KEK) and dataplane DEK-wrapping keys. control plane key = smallest admin surface. dataplane keys per-cluster or per-tenant depending on isolation requirements.
Becky (platform): If per-tenant keys are too many, consider per-customer DEK prefix + key-id mapping in metadata store. important: always require EncryptionContext with tenant id and component.
Theo (sre): Agree on EncryptionContext. Also we need to export KMS API call metadata to SIEM (CloudTrail -> Kinesis -> SIEM). include the encryption context in SIEM events so paging can filter by tenant.
Lina (sec-engineer): BYOK flow question: customers might provide a CMK in their account. How do we safely get access without key policy widening?
Rahul (infra): Use cross-account CreateGrant pattern: customer adds a key policy allowing our service principal to call CreateGrant, or we request a one-time CreateGrant with customer consent. store grant ID and revoke when offboarding. avoid editing the customer's key policy to be permissive.
Becky (platform): Add a preflight verifier: check key policy, validate alias format, run a test re-encrypt handshake using a one-off grant, and require a signed onboarding manifest from the customer.
Theo (sre): Also capture KMS errors and expose a specific alert: high rate of AccessDenied or IncorrectKeyUsage errors during onboarding => potential policy mismatch.
ops-bot: "onboard-byo job queued for account 987654321098"
Lina (sec-engineer): RBAC specifics: control-plane role should have kms:ReEncrypt*, kms:DescribeKey, kms:GetPublicKey (if asymmetric), kms:DisableKey, kms:EnableKey on the control-plane CMK only. dataplane node role: kms:Decrypt/kms:Encrypt for DEK operations, limited by EncryptionContext and source VPC endpoint.
Rahul (infra): Use condition keys: `aws:SourceVpce` to lock KMS usage to our VPC endpoints. also `kms:EncryptionContext:tenant` equality checks.
Becky (platform): Grants vs key policy: prefer CreateGrant for runtime operations (short lived) and keep key policy narrow for principals that manage keys. infrastructure creates grants at cluster startup and revokes at teardown.
Lina (sec-engineer): Rotation and rewrap ops: for keys we own, enable automatic rotation where possible. rotation process: generate new CMK -> create grant/policy -> run re-encrypt of DEKs (no plaintext leak) -> swap pointer -> retire old CMK. provide dry-run first.
Theo (sre): Important: monitor ReEncrypt counts and latencies. spikes may indicate misconfigured batch jobs or malicious mass rewrap attempts. add pager if re-encrypt error rate > 5% within 15m for production.
Becky (platform): sample rewrap command (pseudo): ```bash
aws kms re-encrypt \
  --ciphertext-blob fileb://enc-dek.bin \
  --source-region us-west-2 \
  --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/NEW-KEK-ID \
  --destination-encryption-context '{"component":"dataplane","tenant":"t-123"}'
```
Lina (sec-engineer): Incident playbook highlights: 1) If key suspected compromised: DisableKey (not Delete), revoke grants, create emergency KEK, run rewrap to emergency KEK for affected tenants, rotate service credentials. 2) Preserve CloudTrail logs, snapshot affected S3 prefixes, notify legal.
Rahul (infra): Note: ScheduleKeyDeletion irreversible after waiting period; avoid unless confirmed. prefer DisableKey + audit + rewrap.
Theo (sre): For automation: implement a staging rewrap run that does a dry-run verify (re-encrypt -> attempt decrypt under staging KEK in isolated worker) then only promote after smoke tests pass. include per-tenant progress metrics and ETA.
Becky (platform): Telemetry: we should emit events: rewrap.started, rewrap.progress (count), rewrap.completed, rewrap.failed with tenant id and job id. store these in a searchable ops index.
audit-bot: "CloudTrail forwarding: kms.amazonaws.com events -> secure-bucket (mfa-delete=true) -> kafka topic 'kms-audit'"
Lina (sec-engineer): Vulnerability triage: if a credential leak exposes an EC2 role with kms:GetKeyPolicy, treat as high severity. steps: revoke role sessions, rotate keys where feasible, run integrity checks on ciphertexts, check for unexpected CreateGrant calls.
Rahul (infra): CreateGrant auditing: log grant IDs and attach to cluster metadata so we can enumerate and revoke grants fast. use `RetiringPrincipal` for grants we create so that keys can be retired programmatically.
Becky (platform): Tests: add e2e scenarios in staging: BYOK onboarding, missing encryption context, VPC endpoint blocked, KMS throttling, and rewrap dry-run failures. simulate key disablement and verify graceful failure modes.
Theo (sre): Degradation behavior: control-plane ops should fail fast if KEK unavailable (no stale reads). dataplane inference: allow local DEK cache with strict TTL (e.g., 5 minutes) to handle transient KMS outage for a short window. log cache hits for audit.
Lina (sec-engineer): Example key policy snippet for control-plane CMK (trimmed): ```json
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[
    {"Sid":"AllowControlPlane","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-controlplane"},"Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:ReEncrypt*","kms:DescribeKey"],"Resource":"*","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"kms:EncryptionContext:component":"controlplane"}}}
  ]
}
```
Rahul (infra): Action items: Rahul -> key templates + VPC endpoint examples. Becky -> BYOK onboarding checklist + signed manifest format. Theo -> SIEM mapping + ReEncrypt alerts. Lina -> incident playbook + RBAC diff PR.
ops-bot: "Tasks created: KMS-KEY-TEMPLATES, BYOK-ONBOARD, SIEM-MAPPINGS, KMS-PLAYBOOK"
Lina (sec-engineer): Thanks. I'll draft the PRs and link here. if anyone wants to pair on the rewrap runner, ping me.
